canonical_data: chat sessions and compressed summaries as session files, extracted knowledge triples as a local JSON file mirrored into an optional Neo4j graph or a hosted memory service, and settings in a local config file
strengths: Long conversations are compressed into a six-part persisted summary that carries facts, preferences, decisions and open to-dos into later sessions, and extracted knowledge triples are mirrored to a local file as well as to an optional graph database

Tools are reached through pluggable MCP agents discovered from manifests plus an embedded OpenClaw gateway, and tool calls are parsed from text so any OpenAI-compatible provider works, with an Anthropic-format switch
A dated changelog shows frequent releases across Windows, macOS and Linux packaging, with the OpenClaw runtime bundled into the installer
weaknesses: The code is under AGPL-3.0 with a separate proprietary licence required in writing for closed-source use, a vendored OpenClaw tree is MIT, and the default login path routes model calls and search through the maintainer's hosted gateway
No approval or confirmation step was found in the tool loop, so tool and OpenClaw computer-control calls run without a human gate beyond the round limit
A telemetry queue with an optional upload path ships in the backend, and the test directory holds three test files against a very large codebase
Documentation is Chinese-first, and the product centres on an anime companion persona, which narrows it as a general-purpose workspace
why_it_matters: A rare open desktop assistant that combines a persistent character, graph memory, MCP tools and an embedded delegated-computer runtime in one installable app, under a dual copyleft and proprietary licence.
